content.text: {"candidates":[{"id":"E10","hypothesis_id":"H02","title":"Matched TEA/TEOA photophysics-to-products correlation in the Co-bpy baseline, with optional homogeneous bridge","purpose":"Test whether TEA-versus-TEOA substitution changes donor-side quenching or transient reduced-state observables in the same direction as any CO/H2 shift under otherwise matched conditions, while bounding conclusions if photophysical and catalytic changes decouple.","evidence_ids":["EV053","EV065","EV007","EV081","GX007"],"source_to_proposal":"Sources support donor-dependent quenching measurements and show that donor identity can change irradiation-time photochemical behavior, while catalytic systems require CO and H2 to be quantified together with catalyst-free background controls. The proposal transfers these observations into a matched TEA-versus-TEOA comparison in the recommended Co-bpy platform, and optionally into the supplementary homogeneous cobalt/Ru platform for a cleaner donor-side bridge. This is a proposed correlation test, not proof that any observed photophysical change is the sole cause of selectivity.","groups":[{"id":"E10G01","description":"Primary-platform TEOA baseline under catalytic manifold this is a necessity/background contrast rather than a donor-side causal test."},{"group_a":"E10G02","group_b":"E10G04","changed_factors":["platform"],"inference":"Assesses cobalt-dependent contribution under TEA, again as a necessity/background contrast rather than a donor-side causal test."}],"procedure":["Verify a chemically matched P01 baseline from the supplied recommendation, then prepare paired TEA and TEOA formulations with all non-donor components, reactor geometry, gas handling, and analytical workflow held fixed; include cobalt-omission controls and add the optional P02 bridge only after P01 matching is demonstrated.","For each group, collect donor-side photophysical data on the actual reaction mixture or the closest justified sub-mixture: steady-state emission or absorbance changes suitable for quenching analysis, and a transient optical readout assigned only as a reduced-state or charge-carrier proxy after background subtraction and reference checks.","Run matched photocatalysis on the same formulations and quantify both CO and H2 with time-resolved sampling if signal is above detection limits; analyze no-cobalt groups in parallel to estimate donor/photosensitizer/support background contributions.","Compare the direction, reproducibility, and qualitative magnitude ordering of donor-dependent photophysical changes against donor-dependent CO/H2 changes across replicate runs; if used, test whether the same direction holds in the P02 bridge without assuming mechanistic identity across platforms."],"measurements":["CO amount and H2 amount from the same gas-analysis workflow; derived selectivity reported only as a transformation of measured products, not as a sole readout.","Emission intensity or lifetime changes of the light-absorbing component versus donor identity for matched sub-mixtures; this reports quenching behavior but cannot alone identify the exact quencher or catalytic intermediate.","Transient absorbance or equivalent time-resolved optical signal assigned to a reduced-state or charge-carrier proxy using references/backgrounds; this can indicate donor-dependent formation or persistence of a transient species but cannot by itself establish the active cobalt state.","Background product formation in cobalt-omission groups to bound donor/photosensitizer/support contributions.","If the optional bridge is used, the same classes of photophysical readouts and product measurements in P02 to test directionality transfer only."],"supports":"H02 is supported if, across matched TEA and TEOA runs in P01, donor substitution produces a reproducible shift in at least one donor-side quenching or transient reduced-state observable and the catalytic CO/H2 output changes in the same directional sense, while cobalt-omission controls do not fully account for the product shift. Agreement in direction in the optional P02 bridge would strengthen but not prove transfer.","refutes":"H02 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give similar donor-side quenching and transient observables within experimental resolution in P01, yet CO/H2 differs reproducibly beyond the bounded background seen in cobalt-omission controls. That outcome would favor downstream explanations such as proton-management, catalyst-state, or substrate-binding differences.","inconclusive":"The result is inconclusive if P01 TEA and TEOA cannot be matched reproducibly, if photophysical signals are below assignment confidence or dominated by scattering/support artifacts, if background product formation is too large to isolate cobalt-dependent behavior, or if multiple observables shift in inconsistent directions so that no clear photophysics-to-products correspondence can be established.","parameter_selection":"Do not invent donor concentration, catalyst loading, light intensity, or sampling times. Start from the literature-anchored P01 baseline formulation and verify exact values from the supplied system recommendation. Before the full comparison, run a pilot to choose a dilution window that keeps optical signals measurable without changing component identities, confirms linear detector response, and avoids complete inner-filter saturation. Choose catalytic sampling times by first bracketing an early, mid, and later illumination interval where both CO and H2 remain above detection and the no-cobalt control stays interpretable. For the optional P02 bridge, first confirm that the TEOA formulation reproduces the expected quenching observability before introducing TEA as the single-variable comparator.","limitations":"P01 support effects may decouple measured optical observables from the chemically active manifold. A correlation, even if reproducible, does not exclude coupled proton-transfer or cobalt-speciation changes. A lack of correlation may reflect insensitive observables rather than true absence of donor-side differences. Cobalt-omission contrasts are inherently multi-effect necessity tests because omitting cobalt changes the catalytic manifold and may alter background charge recombination. The P02 bridge improves photophysical interpretability but is not chemically identical to the Co-bpy/g-C3N4 target, so only directionality transfer is justified.","feasibility":"moderate"}]}
